heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 2A.2 · Gong Sun Chou I, ch. 2
Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 2A.7 · Gong Sun Chou I, ch. 7 … Gong Sun Chou II, ch. 1
Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 2B.9 · Gong Sun Chou II, ch. 9 … Gong Sun Chou II, ch. 12
Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 1B.4 · Liang Hui Wang II, ch. 4 … Liang Hui Wang II, ch. 5
Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 2A.3 · Gong Sun Chou I, ch. 3 … Gong Sun Chou I, ch. 6

items.text: Develop the four principles in yourself, that you may serve your parents.
items.quote: they will not suffice for a man to serve his parents with.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 1A.7 · Liang Hui Wang I, ch. 7

items.text: Serve your parents: provide for them sufficiently so they lack nothing needed.
items.citation: Mencius, Liang Hui Wang I, ch. 7
items.quote: sufficient wherewith to serve their parents

items.text: Support your wife, providing for her needs.
items.citation: Mencius, Liang Hui Wang I, ch. 7
items.quote: support their wives

items.text: Support your children, providing for their needs.
items.citation: Mencius, Liang Hui Wang I, ch. 7
items.quote: support their children

items.text: Fulfill your fraternal duty: honor and obey your elder siblings.
items.citation: Mencius, Liang Hui Wang I, ch. 7
items.quote: fraternal duties

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 2B.4 · Gong Sun Chou II, ch. 4 … Gong Sun Chou II, ch. 8

items.text: Provide a generous coffin and burial for your deceased parents, not being niggardly; this satisfies natural feeling and keeps the earth from their bodies.
items.quote: I have heard that the superior man will not for all the world be niggardly to his parents.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 1B.16 · Liang Hui Wang II, ch. 16 … Gong Sun Chou I, ch. 1

items.text: Observe the mourning rites for a deceased parent according to propriety and your means; do not let richer observances cause you to exceed what is fitting.
items.quote: That was the difference between being poor and being rich.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 2B.2 · Gong Sun Chou II, ch. 2 … Gong Sun Chou II, ch. 3

items.text: Let kindness be the ruling principle in your relation with your son.
items.citation: Mencius, Gong Sun Chou II, ch. 2
items.quote: Between father and son the ruling principle is kindness.

items.text: When your father calls, answer immediately, without a moment's hesitation.
items.citation: Mencius, Gong Sun Chou II, ch. 2
items.quote: When a father calls, the answer must be without a moment's hesitation.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 3A.3 · Teng Wen Gong I, ch. 3

items.text: Nourish your parents; do not let them go hungry after a year's toil.
items.quote: after the whole year's toil, yet not to be able to nourish their parents

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 1A.1 · Liang Hui Wang I, ch. 1 … Liang Hui Wang I, ch. 3

items.text: Do not neglect your parents.
items.quote: There never has been a benevolent man who neglected his parents.

items.text: Practice filial piety toward your parents.
items.quote: inculcating in it especially the filial and fraternal duties

items.text: Practice fraternal duty toward your elder siblings: respect and obey them.
items.quote: inculcating in it especially the filial and fraternal duties

items.text: Nourish your living parents.
items.quote: nourish their living and mourn for their dead

items.text: Mourn for your dead parents and bury them properly.
items.quote: mourn for their dead

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 3A.5 · Teng Wen Gong I, ch. 5 … Teng Wen Gong II, ch. 2

items.text: Give your parents a proper burial when they die.
items.quote: the filial son and virtuous man, in interring in a handsome manner their parents, act according to a proper rule

items.text: Respect and obey your husband.
items.quote: You must be respectful; you must be careful. Do not disobey your husband.

items.text: Admonish her at her marriage to be respectful and to obey her husband.
items.quote: At the marrying away of a young woman, her mother admonishes her, accompanying her to the door on her leaving

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 5B.1 · Wan Zhang II, ch. 1
Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 3B.8 · Teng Wen Gong II, ch. 8 … Teng Wen Gong II, ch. 9

items.text: Give your father the peculiar affection due to him; do not deny it by loving all equally.
items.citation: Mencius, Teng Wen Gong II, ch. 9
items.quote: Mo's principle is 'to love all equally,' which does not acknowledge the peculiar affection due to a father.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 1B.6 · Liang Hui Wang II, ch. 6 … Liang Hui Wang II, ch. 10

items.text: Care for the wife entrusted to you, and do not let her suffer cold or hunger.
items.quote: entrust his wife and children to the care of his friend... let his wife and children suffer from cold and hunger

items.text: Care for the children entrusted to you, and do not let them suffer cold or hunger.
items.quote: entrust his wife and children to the care of his friend... let his wife and children suffer from cold and hunger

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 5B.4 · Wan Zhang II, ch. 4 … Wan Zhang II, ch. 5
Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 5B.7 · Wan Zhang II, ch. 7 … Gaozi I, ch. 1
Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 5A.7 · Wan Zhang I, ch. 7 … Wan Zhang I, ch. 9
Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 3A.4 · Teng Wen Gong I, ch. 4

items.text: Cherish your son with fatherly affection.
items.quote: between father and son, there should be affection

items.text: Cherish your father with filial affection.
items.quote: between father and son, there should be affection

items.text: Perform your proper duties as husband, giving yourself to your own work in the household.
items.quote: between husband and wife, attention to their separate functions

items.text: Perform your proper duties as wife, giving yourself to your own work in the household.
items.quote: between husband and wife, attention to their separate functions

items.text: Yield to your elders and keep the order proper between old and young.
items.quote: between old and young, a proper order

items.text: Guide the young and keep the order proper between old and young.
items.quote: between old and young, a proper order

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 6A.6 · Gaozi I, ch. 6 … Gaozi I, ch. 7
Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 6A.8 · Gaozi I, ch. 8 … Gaozi I, ch. 13
Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 5B.6 · Wan Zhang II, ch. 6
Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 3B.5 · Teng Wen Gong II, ch. 5 … Teng Wen Gong II, ch. 7

items.text: Offer the proper sacrifices; do not neglect them as the chief of Ge did.
items.quote: neglecting his proper sacrifices

items.text: Employ for your son a teacher of what you intend him to learn, and keep him from those who would teach him otherwise.
items.quote: employ a man of Qi as his tutor

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 1A.7 · Liang Hui Wang I, ch. 7

items.text: Treat with reverence the elders in your own family.
items.quote: Treat with the reverence due to age the elders in your own family

items.text: Treat with kindness the young in your own family.
items.quote: treat with the kindness due to youth the young in your own family

items.text: Protect your wife.
items.quote: he will not be able to protect his wife and children

items.text: Protect your children.
items.quote: he will not be able to protect his wife and children

items.text: Show kindness to your brothers.
items.quote: It reached to his brothers

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 1B.1 · Liang Hui Wang II, ch. 1 … Liang Hui Wang II, ch. 3

items.text: Share your pleasures and enjoyments with those under your care; do not keep them to yourself while they suffer.
items.citation: Mencius, Liang Hui Wang II, ch. 1
items.quote: make pleasure a thing common to the people and yourself

items.text: Allow those under your care free access to the resources of the land; do not fence them off for your private enjoyment.
items.citation: Mencius, Liang Hui Wang II, ch. 2
items.quote: He shared it with the people

items.text: Govern so that families under your authority are not separated or scattered, but may remain together in peace.
items.citation: Mencius, Liang Hui Wang II, ch. 1
items.quote: Fathers and sons cannot see one another... separated and scattered abroad

items.text: Use your strength and righteous anger to give peace and security to all under your care, not to oppress or terrify them.
items.citation: Mencius, Liang Hui Wang II, ch. 3
items.quote: in one burst of anger, give repose to all the people of the kingdom

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 4A.2 · Li Lou I, ch. 2 … Li Lou I, ch. 8

items.text: Be benevolent, that you may preserve the ancestral temple from ruin.
items.quote: If a high noble or great officer be not benevolent, he cannot preserve his ancestral temple.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the first and second commandments; we honor parents but do not offer sacrifices to the dead.
items.needs_role: high noble or great officer (大夫)

items.text: Rule the household by correcting your own person, for the root of the family is in its head.
items.quote: The root of the family is in the person of its Head.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 1A.4 · Liang Hui Wang I, ch. 4 … Liang Hui Wang I, ch. 6

items.text: Support your parents in their old age and need; do not let them suffer cold or hunger.
items.citation: Mencius, Liang Hui Wang I, chs. 4–6
items.quote: in order to support their parents. Their parents suffer from cold and hunger.

items.text: Respect and serve your elder brother with fraternal deference.
items.citation: Mencius, Liang Hui Wang I, chs. 4–6
items.quote: serving thereby, at home, their fathers and elder brothers

items.text: Serve and honor those older and above you, both at home and abroad.
items.citation: Mencius, Liang Hui Wang I, chs. 4–6
items.quote: serving thereby, at home, their fathers and elder brothers, and, abroad, their elders and superiors

items.text: Do not bring shame on your ancestors; if you have, strive to wipe away the disgrace.
items.citation: Mencius, Liang Hui Wang I, chs. 4–6
items.quote: I have brought shame on my departed predecessors, and wish on their account to wipe it away.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 7B.38 · Jin Xin II, ch. 38
Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 6B.11 · Gaozi II, ch. 11 … Jin Xin I, ch. 7
Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 6B.5 · Gaozi II, ch. 5 … Gaozi II, ch. 6
Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 4B.23 · Li Lou II, ch. 23 … Li Lou II, ch. 29

items.text: Love others and show them respect; when treated badly, first examine your own conduct.
items.quote: The benevolent man loves others. The man of propriety shows respect to others.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 5A.3 · Wan Zhang I, ch. 3 … Wan Zhang I, ch. 4

items.text: Do not harbor anger or resentment against your brother; regard him with affection and love, wishing him honor and wealth.
items.quote: A benevolent man does not lay up anger, nor cherish resentment against his brother, but only regards him with affection and love.

items.text: Honor and support your parents with all you possess; this is the greatest duty of a son.
items.quote: Of all which a filial son can attain to, there is nothing greater than his honouring his parents.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 3B.10 · Teng Wen Gong II, ch. 10 … Li Lou I, ch. 1

items.text: Do not leave your mother; stay near and serve her.
items.quote: Avoiding his brother and leaving his mother, he went and dwelt in Wu Ling.

items.text: Eat what your mother gives you; do not reject her food.
items.quote: Thus, what his mother gave him he would not eat, but what his wife gives him he eats.

items.text: Do not shun your elder brother; remain on good terms with him.
items.quote: Avoiding his brother and leaving his mother, he went and dwelt in Wu Ling.

items.text: Assist your husband by your labor to provide for the household.
items.quote: his wife twists and dresses threads of hemp to sell or exchange them

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 4A.9 · Li Lou I, ch. 9 … Li Lou I, ch. 17

items.text: Love your parents.
items.quote: If each man would love his parents

items.text: Serve your parents so as to make them pleased.
items.quote: serve his parents so as to make them pleased

items.text: Show due respect to your elders.
items.quote: show the due respect to his elders

items.text: Rescue your drowning sister-in-law even if it means touching her hand, though that is normally forbidden.
items.quote: He who would not so rescue the drowning woman is a wolf

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 2B.13 · Gong Sun Chou II, ch. 13 … Teng Wen Gong I, ch. 2

items.text: Serve your parents according to propriety while they are alive.
items.citation: Mencius, Teng Wen Gong I, ch. 2
items.quote: When parents are alive, they should be served according to propriety

items.text: Bury your parents according to propriety when they are dead.
items.citation: Mencius, Teng Wen Gong I, ch. 2
items.quote: when they are dead, they should be buried according to propriety

items.text: Offer sacrifices to your parents according to propriety when they are dead.
items.citation: Mencius, Teng Wen Gong I, ch. 2
items.quote: they should be sacrificed to according to propriety
items.conflict: Ancestor sacrifice conflicts with the first commandment to worship God alone (Exodus 20:3).

items.text: Observe the three years' mourning for your parents.
items.citation: Mencius, Teng Wen Gong I, ch. 2
items.quote: the three years' mourning... were equally prescribed by the three dynasties, and binding on all

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 4B.3 · Li Lou II, ch. 3 … Li Lou II, ch. 22

items.text: Train your children in the Mean and in the abilities you possess, so that they may rejoice in having a father of virtue and talent.
items.quote: Those who keep the Mean, train up those who do not.

items.text: Train your younger siblings in the Mean and in the abilities you possess, so that they may rejoice in having an elder brother of virtue and talent.
items.quote: Those who keep the Mean, train up those who do not.

items.text: Nourish your parents while they live; do not consider it the greatest thing, for greater is yet to come.
items.quote: The nourishment of parents when living is not sufficient to be accounted the great thing.

items.text: Perform your parents' obsequies when they die; do this as the greater duty, surpassing their nourishment in life.
items.quote: It is only in the performing their obsequies when dead that we have what can be considered the great thing.
items.conflict: Conflicts with biblical prohibition of ancestor worship and communication with the dead.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 1B.11 · Liang Hui Wang II, ch. 11 … Liang Hui Wang II, ch. 15

items.text: Do not be negligent or cruel to those under you; when they are in distress, tell them and use your stores to relieve them.
items.quote: your granaries, 0 prince, have been stored with grain, and your treasuries and arsenals have been full, and not one of your officers has told you of the distress.

items.text: Lay the foundation of the inheritance and hand down what your successors may continue; be strong to do good.
items.quote: A prince lays the foundation of the inheritance, and hands down the beginning which he has made, doing what may be continued by his successors.

items.text: Do not injure your children with what you should use to nourish them; if remaining would harm them, leave rather than cause them harm.
items.quote: a ruler does not injure his people with that wherewith he nourishes them. My children, why should you be troubled about having no prince?
items.needs_role: ruler as father of his people

items.text: Do not dispose of the family inheritance on your own; keep it intact for the generations, even to death.
items.quote: The kingdom is a thing to be kept from generation to generation. One individual cannot undertake to dispose of it in his own person. Let him be prepared to die for it.
items.needs_role: prince as head of his house

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 5A.1 · Wan Zhang I, ch. 1 … Wan Zhang I, ch. 2

items.text: Do not murmur when your parents punish you; continue to love and remember them.
items.quote: When his parents hate him, though they punish him, he does not murmur.

items.text: Keep your desire towards your parents to the end of your life, above all other attachments.
items.quote: The man of great filial piety, to the end of his life, has his desire towards his parents.

items.text: Inform your parents before taking a wife.
items.quote: In marrying a wife, how ought a man to proceed? He must inform his parents.

items.text: Dwell together with your wife, for this is the greatest of human relations.
items.quote: That male and female should dwell together, is the greatest of human relations.

items.text: Rejoice in your younger brother's presence and do not hold his evil against him.
items.quote: When Xiang was sorrowful, he was also sorrowful; when Xiang was joyful, he was also joyful.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 7A.8 · Jin Xin I, ch. 8 … Jin Xin I, ch. 21

items.text: Love your parents; filial affection for parents is the working of benevolence.
items.quote: Children carried in the arms all know to love their parents

items.text: Love your elder brothers; respect for elders is the working of righteousness.
items.quote: when they are grown a little, they all know to love their elder brothers

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 5B.2 · Wan Zhang II, ch. 2 … Wan Zhang II, ch. 3

items.text: Show respect to those above you as the observance due to their rank requires.
items.quote: Respect shown by inferiors to superiors is called giving to the noble the observance due to rank.

items.text: Honor the virtue and talent of those below you.
items.quote: Respect shown by superiors to inferiors is called giving honour to talents and virtue.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 6B.2 · Gaozi II, ch. 2 … Gaozi II, ch. 4

items.text: Walk slowly behind your elders, and do not go ahead of them.
items.quote: To walk slowly, keeping behind his elders, is to perform the part of a younger.

items.text: Serve your father out of benevolence and righteousness, never from thoughts of profit.
items.quote: sons will serve their fathers, cherishing the principles of benevolence and righteousness

items.text: Serve your elder brother out of benevolence and righteousness, never from thoughts of profit.
items.quote: younger brothers will serve their elder brothers, in the same way

items.text: Be grieved at a parent's serious fault, but do not fret over a small one; both indifference and unnecessary murmuring are unfilial.
items.quote: To increase the want of natural affection would have been unfilial, and to fret and foam in such a manner would also have been unfilial.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 5A.5 · Wan Zhang I, ch. 5 … Wan Zhang I, ch. 6

items.text: Observe three years' mourning at the death of your father, the sovereign.
items.quote: After the death of Yao, when the three years' mourning was completed

items.text: Reverently pursue the same course as your father.
items.quote: that Qi was able, as a man of talents and virtue, reverently to pursue the same course as Yu

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 6A.14 · Gaozi I, ch. 14 … Gaozi II, ch. 1

items.text: Do not twist your elder brother's arm or snatch his food, even if you would otherwise starve.
items.quote: If, by twisting your elder brother's arm, and snatching from him what he is eating, you can get food for yourself

items.text: Do not get over your neighbour's wall and drag away his daughter to make her your wife, even if you cannot otherwise marry.
items.quote: by getting over your neighbour's wall, and dragging away his virgin daughter, you can get a wife

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 4B.30 · Li Lou II, ch. 30 … Li Lou II, ch. 33

items.text: Attend to the nourishment of your parents; do not through laziness fail to provide for them.
items.quote: The first is laziness in the use of one's four limbs, without attending to the nourishment of his parents.

items.text: Do not waste time and resources on gambling, chess-playing, or wine, but attend to the nourishment of your parents.
items.quote: The second is gambling and chess-playing and being fond of wine, without attending to the nourishment of his parents.

items.text: Do not be fond of goods and money or selfishly attached to your wife and children, so as to neglect the nourishment of your parents.
items.quote: The third is being fond of goods and money, and selfishly attached to his wife and children, without attending to the nourishment of his parents.

items.text: Do not indulge your ears and eyes so as to bring disgrace on your parents.
items.quote: The fourth is following the desires of one's ears and eyes, so as to bring his parents to disgrace.

items.text: Do not be fond of bravery, fighting and quarrelling, lest you endanger your parents.
items.quote: The fifth is being fond of bravery, fighting and quarrelling so as to endanger his parents.

items.text: Do not reprove your father to urge him to what is good, for that is the way of friends and injures the kindness between father and son.
items.quote: To urge one another to what is good by reproofs is the way of friends. But such urging between father and son is the greatest injury to the kindness, which should prevail between them.

items.text: If you have offended your father and are not permitted to approach him, send away your wife and child and receive no cherishing attention from them, for to do otherwise would be a great crime.
items.quote: he sent away his wife, and drove forth his son, and all his life receives no cherishing attention from them.
items.conflict: Husbands must not put away wives except for sexual immorality (Matt 5:32; 19:9); fathers must not abandon children (1 Tim 5:8).

items.text: Seek your living honestly; do not bring shame upon your wife or concubine by beggarly or deceitful conduct.
items.quote: as to the ways by which men seek for riches, honours, gain, and advancement, there are few of their wives and concubines who would not be ashamed and weep together on account of them.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 7A.22 · Jin Xin I, ch. 22 … Jin Xin I, ch. 32

items.text: Nourish your aged parents: keep them warm with silk and feed them meat, so they are not cold or hungry.
items.quote: At fifty, warmth cannot be maintained without silks, and at seventy flesh is necessary to satisfy the appetite.

items.text: As a daughter-in-law, nourish your husband's aged parents with warmth and food.
items.quote: instructing the wives and children, so as to make them nourish their aged.

items.text: Be filial and obedient to your elders.
items.quote: If the young in it follow his instructions, they become filial, obedient to their elders, true-hearted, and faithful.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 7B.32 · Jin Xin II, ch. 32 … Jin Xin II, ch. 37

items.text: Weep for the dead from real sorrow, not to make a show before the living.
items.quote: Weeping for the dead should be from real sorrow, and not because of the living.

items.text: Do not eat what your father especially liked, just as you do not use his personal name.
items.quote: Zeng Xi was fond of sheep-dates, and his son, the philosopher Zeng, could not bear to eat sheep-dates.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 7A.33 · Jin Xin I, ch. 33 … Jin Xin I, ch. 45

items.text: Do not disown your parents or any relatives; to do so is among the greatest crimes.
items.quote: A man can have no greater crimes than to disown his parents and relatives

items.text: Stand by your father even if he has done wrong; give up your own position to protect him and live with him.
items.quote: Shun would have regarded abandoning the kingdom as throwing away a worn-out sandal. He would privately have taken his father on his back

items.text: Do not harm your elder brother; treat him with fraternal duty.
items.quote: as if there were one twisting the arm of his elder brother... teach such an one filial piety and fraternal duty

items.text: Mourn a departed parent for the full period; if prevented, observe at least some days rather than none.
items.quote: The addition of even a single day is better than not mourning at all.

items.text: Be affectionate to your parents above all, loving to people generally, and kind to creatures.
items.quote: He is affectionate to his parents, and lovingly disposed to people generally.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 4A.18 · Li Lou I, ch. 18 … Li Lou II, ch. 2

items.text: Do not reprove your son for what is good; reproofs lead to alienation.
items.quote: Between father and son, there should be no reproving admonitions to what is good. Such reproofs lead to alienation
items.conflict: Fathers are to bring up children in the Lord's nurture and admonition (Eph 6:4).

items.text: Serve your parents as your highest duty; nourish their will, not only their mouth and body.
items.quote: Of services, which is the greatest? The service of parents is the greatest.

items.text: Keep yourself morally upright, for only then can you serve your parents.
items.quote: That those who do not fail to keep themselves are able to serve their parents is what I have heard.

items.text: Do not delay going to see an elder because your lodging is not arranged; visit him first.
items.quote: Have you heard that a scholar's lodging-house must be arranged before he visit his elder?

items.text: Have children to continue the family line; childlessness is the greatest unfilial act.
items.quote: There are three things which are unfilial, and to have no posterity is the greatest of them.

items.text: Inform your parents before you marry; do not marry without their knowledge.
items.quote: Shun married without informing his parents because of this, lest he should have no posterity.

items.text: Obey your elder brothers; that is the richest fruit of righteousness.
items.quote: The richest fruit of righteousness is this: the obeying one's elder brothers.

items.text: Strive for entire accord with your parents and win their hearts; without this you are not a true son.
items.quote: If he could not get to an entire accord with his parents, he could not be considered a son.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 6A.2 · Gaozi I, ch. 2 … Gaozi I, ch. 5

items.text: Give greater respect to your uncle than to your younger brother, for age commands honor.
items.quote: Which do you respect most, your uncle, or your younger brother? He will answer, 'My uncle.'

items.text: Respect your elder brother above an older outsider, for kinship outranks age.
items.quote: to which of them would you show the greater respect? 'To my brother,' was the reply

items.text: When a family member personates an ancestor in the rite, show the greater respect to the ancestor through him.
items.quote: If your younger brother be personating a dead ancestor, to which do you show the greater respect, to him or to your uncle? He will say, 'To my younger brother.'
items.conflict: Conflicts with biblical prohibition of venerating the dead (Deut 18:10-12; Lev 19:28).

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 6B.7 · Gaozi II, ch. 7 … Gaozi II, ch. 10

items.text: Be filial to your parents: obey, serve, and honor them; never be unfilial.
items.quote: Slay the unfilial

items.text: Do not change the son appointed as your heir; keep him in his rightful place.
items.quote: change not the son who has been appointed heir

items.text: Do not exalt a concubine to the position of your wife; let your wife alone have that place.
items.quote: exalt not a concubine to be the wife

items.text: Respect and honor the aged; give them the deference due to their years.
items.quote: Respect the old

items.text: Be kind to the young; treat them with gentleness and care.
items.quote: be kind to the young

items.text: Set aside sufficient resources to maintain the ancestral temple and observe its prescribed rites for your ancestors.
items.quote: observe the statutes kept in his ancestral temple
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration conflicts with the First Commandment: worship belongs to God alone (Exod 20:3-6).

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 3B.3 · Teng Wen Gong II, ch. 3 … Teng Wen Gong II, ch. 4

items.text: Arrange a marriage for your son and daughter through proper go-betweens.
items.quote: When a son is born, what is desired for him is that he may have a wife

items.text: Wait for your parents' orders and the go-between's arrangements before seeking a partner; do not secretly meet.
items.quote: without waiting for the orders of their parents, and the arrangements of the go-betweens, shall bore holes to steal a sight of each other

items.text: Be filial at home: obey and honor your parents.
items.quote: at home, is filial

items.text: Show respect to elders abroad.
items.quote: abroad, respectful to his elders

items.text: Prepare the garments for sacrifice, helping your husband in the rites.
items.quote: His wife keeps silkworms, and unwinds their cocoons, to make the garments for sacrifice.

items.text: Provide the offerings for sacrifice by your own labor; do not presume to sacrifice if they are incomplete.
items.quote: A prince ploughs himself, and is assisted by the people, to supply the millet for sacrifice.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 7B.17 · Jin Xin II, ch. 17 … Jin Xin II, ch. 31

items.text: Love your son with natural affection; this bond is part of your Heaven-endowed nature, not merely fate.
items.quote: The exercise of love between father and son... these are the appointment of Heaven.

items.text: Love your father with natural affection; this bond is part of your Heaven-endowed nature, not merely fate.
items.quote: The exercise of love between father and son... these are the appointment of Heaven.

heading: Mencius 孟子 · The Works of Mencius (Legge) · Mencius 7A.46 · Jin Xin I, ch. 46 … Jin Xin II, ch. 16

items.text: Keep the full three years' mourning for your father and mother.
items.quote: Not to be able to keep the three years' mourning, and to be very particular about that of three months, or that of five months

items.text: Do not sacrifice your son or expose him to death for your own gain.
items.quote: urged his son whom he loved till he sacrificed him with them

items.text: Walk in the right path and order rightly, so that your wife will follow and obey.
items.quote: If a man himself do not walk in the right path, it will not be walked in even by his wife and children.

items.text: Walk in the right path and order rightly, so that your children will follow and obey.
items.quote: If he order men according to what is not the right way, he will not be able to get the obedience of even his wife and children.
